name: 3D modelling, texturing and rendering
one_line: A 3D asset lifecycle joining a brief or build record to model, material, rig, scene or render sources, versioned review, delivery manifests and evidenced use rights; an isolated model or rendered image is not enough.

deterministic: a labelled brief, ticket or statement of work that identifies an asset purpose, requested deliverable, source package and reviewer or recipient, followed by matching 3D source or output evidence
a manifest or scene README that joins model geometry, material/texture dependencies, rigs or cameras, exports and a stable asset identifier
a review packet naming exact asset versions or render outputs, recording requested changes, and linking to a later revision or acceptance record
a delivery packet with an asset manifest, dependency/license notes, recipient or destination, and an explicit handoff or acceptance record
a rights or usage record naming the asset or package and permitting a stated game, film, product, architectural, marketing, or publication use
needs_llm: deciding whether a model is a creative asset, BIM/construction model, engineering/manufacturing model, scientific visualization, game asset, or code-generated output
matching differently named source scenes, textures, caches, exports and previews when manifests, embedded links, metadata or review references establish one asset family
deciding whether a render is an authored output, supplied client material, downloaded reference, portfolio image, photograph, or screenshot
deciding whether a review, delivery, acceptance, or license applies to the whole package or only named files, variants, platforms, territories, or time windows
deciding whether an archive member inherits package context; archive paths and neighboring files do not by themselves write facts onto every member
never_alone: a filename containing model, asset, mesh, texture, rig, render, scene, final, v02, approved, export or delivery
a software name, renderer name, folder called Assets/Models/Renders, version suffix, timestamp, or download session
a single 3D file, preview, turntable, render, screenshot, texture sheet, or cache without an evidenced purpose and source/review/delivery relationship
visual similarity, a public asset-library page, missing EXIF, a client/studio name, or an author field without role-bearing lifecycle evidence
a repository, procedural script, CAD/BIM title block, manufacturing drawing, or game build without the creative asset chain

grouping_reasons: one named asset from brief or request through source files, dependencies, previews, review revisions and delivery
one version family when stable asset identifiers, manifests or review references join successive revisions
one dependency set when textures, fonts, HDRIs, meshes, caches and licenses are explicitly referenced by the scene or manifest
one handoff when the manifest, exported package, recipient and acceptance/use record refer to the same asset release
no group for an isolated render, downloaded stock model, unrelated cache, public reference, or repository whose object is code

template.why: The creative schema declares no field rows, so no folder dimensions are legal at launch. Asset name, stage, software, renderer, format, platform, polygon budget and delivery channel remain values or retrieval metadata until a future creative schema decision. The lifecycle is not time-first: build, review, delivery and use rights can have separate clocks.

collides_with.signal: Both may contain meshes, textures, rigs, exports and platform manifests; game-art owns interactive/game-engine evidence, while this row covers a broader 3D source-to-review-to-handoff chain.
Procedural generators, repositories and build scripts can produce meshes; code owns the repository and executable workflow when the asset lifecycle is not independently evidenced.
Rendered stills, turntables and screenshots are image or video files; photos owns photographic capture evidence, while this row requires authored 3D source or manifest lineage.
CAD/BIM models may be 3D files with revisions; controlled title blocks, tolerances, issue status and construction transmittals indicate the construction domain rather than creative asset production.
A license or release may name a 3D asset; rights owns the governing rights instrument, while this row activates only when the instrument joins a specific asset lifecycle.
A portfolio may display the same render or model; career owns capability presentation when the local build/review/delivery chain is absent.

falls_through_to.why: A brief, manifest, model or delivery record without a recoverable asset chain remains a standalone record.
Unjoined versions, ambiguous model types and unsupported approval claims require review.
An isolated render, turntable frame or screenshot without source lineage is an image.
Downloaded reference models, texture libraries and tutorials are consumed material.
A standalone signed license, acceptance, release or rights schedule remains protected evidence.
Unreadable proprietary scenes or encrypted archives cannot establish the lifecycle chain.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased designs, client briefs, source geometry, licensed textures or HDRIs, proprietary techniques, recipient information, product or security models, and restricted usage terms may be sensitive. A public-looking render does not prove public permission.
open_question: NJ-3D-1: Should a future creative schema expose a compact project/stage/artifact_type set for 3D asset lifecycles, or remain fieldless? Recommendation: preserve this placeholder until that schema decision. NJ-3D-2: When a 3D asset is both a general creative deliverable and a game-engine asset, should the two templates co-hold on one source package or activate independently by purpose evidence?
